summary.value: The Onagadori, whose Japanese name means long-tailed chicken, comes from the old Tosa Province, now Kochi Prefecture on the island of Shikoku. Breeders there created it in the 1600s from other long-tailed Japanese fowl, and it is still raised mainly around Nankoku. Its fame rests on a tail of 16 to 18 feathers that, in the right conditions, never molt and keep growing by roughly 2 to 4 feet a year. Tails pass 5 feet as a matter of course, and a few have been reported at close to 40 feet. Japan recognizes three colors, the oldest being white with a black breast, and British clubs recognize five. The bird has a single comb and white earlobes. It is kept only for ornament, in tall hutches that hold the tail off the ground. Japan named it a Special Natural Treasure in 1952, and only a few hundred birds remain.
